pairs: Utinam appenderentur peccata mea quibus iram merui,
I wish that my sins, for which I deserve wrath,
et calamitas quam patior, in statera!
and the calamity that I endure, were weighed out on a balance.
Quasi arena maris hæc gravior appareret;
Compared to the sand of the sea,
et verba mea dolore sunt plena:
and so my words are full of sorrow.
quia sagittæ Domini in me sunt,
For the arrows of the Lord are in me,
my spirit drinks of their indignation,
et terrores Domini militant contra me.
and the terrors of the Lord are soldiers against me.
Numquid rugiet onager cum habuerit herbam?
Will the wild ass bray when he has grass?
aut mugiet bos cum ante præsepe plenum steterit?
Or will the ox bellow when he stands before a full manger?
Or can one eat bland food,
which is not seasoned with salt?
aut potest aliquis gustare quod gustatum affert mortem?
Or can anyone taste that which, if tasted, causes death?
Quæ prius nolebat tangere anima mea,
The things that my soul was unwilling to touch before,
Quis det ut veniat petitio mea,
Who will grant that my petition may arrive
et quod expecto tribuat mihi Deus?
and that God may bestow on me what I expect,
will let loose his hand and cut me down?
And may this be my consolation,
that in afflicting me with sorrow,
although he might not be lenient with me,
I still do not contradict the words of the Holy One.
so that I may act patiently?
My strength is not the strength of stones,
nor is my flesh made of bronze.
Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me,
Behold, there is no help for me in myself,
et necessarii quoque mei recesserunt a me.
and my loved ones also have withdrawn from me.
Qui tollit ab amico suo misericordiam,
He who takes away mercy from his friend,
abandons the fear of the Lord.
sicut torrens qui raptim transit in convallibus.
like a torrent that passes swiftly through the steep valleys.
At that time, when they are scattered,
they will be freed from their place.
The paths of their steps are entangled;
They have been thrown into confusion,
they have even come to me
and merely by seeing my affliction,
et de substantia vestra donate mihi?
and give to me from your necessities?”
“Free me from the hand of the enemy
et de manu robustorum eruite me?
and rescue me from the hand of the strong?”
and if by chance I have been ignorant of anything,
Why have you diminished the words of truth,
cum e vobis nullus sit qui possit arguere me?
when there is none of you who is able to offer proof against me?
You prepare speeches as so much noise,
and you offer words into the wind.
and you strive to undermine your friend.
Such is true, so finish what you have begun.
et loquentes id quod justum est,
Et non invenietis in lingua mea iniquitatem,
And you will not find iniquity on my tongue,
nec in faucibus meis stultitia personabit.
nor will foolishness resound in my throat.
